candidatos.titulo: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
candidatos.autores: Stephen Chung, Wenyu Du
candidatos.resumo: Many recent open-weight language models use n-gram embedding tables to improve performance. These tables store learned representations of short token sequences, such as pairs or triples of consecutive tokens, which the model retrieves during processing. However, they can require substantial memory: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, for example, allocates 196 billion parameters to its Engram n-gram memory. We therefore investigate whether this memory cost can be reduced while preserving the performance improvement that the tables provide. candidatos.titulo: Extreme Compression of Per-Layer Embeddings via Cross-Layer Latent Vector Quantization
candidatos.autores: Jiacheng Liu, Yaxin Luo, Xiaohan Zhao, Peng Sun, Xinyi Shang, Jiacheng Cui
candidatos.resumo: Scaling embedding capacity alongside Transformer computation is an emerging trend in language models. This trend makes high compression rates increasingly useful. Hence, we study extreme compression of Per-Layer Embeddings (PLE), which follow this trend and account for 35.2% of the parameters of Gemma 4 E4B. At such rates, conventional quantizers give each token-layer vector its own code of only a few bytes. candidatos.titulo: Lychee: Certified Screening of Inverted Lists for High-Recall Vector Search
candidatos.autores: Dongfang Zhao
candidatos.resumo: Nearest-neighbor search over embedding vectors matches faces against watchlists, transactions against known fraud patterns, and medical images against confirmed cases, where a missed neighbor is a missed threat, fraud, or diagnosis. Because an approximate index cannot report which queries lost a true neighbor, these applications require recall of 0.999 to 0.9999, at a cost far below that of exact search over billions of vectors. candidatos.titulo: GhostFaceMPC: Privacy-Preserving Face Recognition with Multi-Party Computation
candidatos.autores: Davide Carnemolla, Dario Catalano, Mario Di Raimondo
candidatos.resumo: Facial recognition has become central to modern authentication systems, security frameworks, and personalized services. However, its widespread adoption is hindered by severe privacy risks, particularly surrounding unauthorized access to sensitive biometric data. To address these challenges, this paper presents GhostFaceMPC, the first end-to-end, privacy-preserving face recognition system to evaluate a deep convolutional neural network extractor and matching under secure multi-party computation. candidatos.titulo: Compressing Onboard Language Models for Space Robots under a Behavioral-Fidelity Requirement
candidatos.autores: Jia Deng, Zizhe Wang, Xin Lu, Yi Huang, Zehao Jia
candidatos.resumo: Language models are being explored as the interface through which space robots interpret operator commands and select among verified skills. Running them onboard calls for low-bit compression, and flight use adds requirements that generic post-training quantization leaves implicit: a fixed memory budget and storage format, a static artifact under configuration control, and behavior close to the full-precision model validated on the ground. candidatos.titulo: ACE-Compression: An Ability-Centric Evaluation of Compressed Large Language Models
candidatos.autores: Jiahui Ning, Liang Chen, Yuchen Liang, Yi Zhang, Fenglei Fan
candidatos.resumo: Model compression makes large language models deployable, but today's evaluation tells an incomplete story. Standard practice measures retained task performance and stops there. This misses a critical fact: compression perturbs the distributed knowledge embedded across billions of weights, and task scores alone cannot reveal which underlying abilities survive and which quietly collapse. candidatos.titulo: Provable Adversarial Detection: Prime Quantization meets Gromov--Wasserstein
candidatos.autores: Manohar Kaul, Sadbhavana Babar, Aditya Ramesh, Aditya Saibewar, Fumiyoshi Kasahara, Maki Inui
candidatos.resumo: Adversarial vulnerability persists across modern vision architectures from CNNs to vision language models (VLMs), yet existing detection methods rely on heuristics without theoretical guarantees. We address the fundamental question of when adversarial perturbations can be provably detected from a geometric perspective. candidatos.titulo: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pairs: finite presentations and graded coideal structures
candidatos.autores: Jian-Rong Li, Tomasz Przezdziecki
candidatos.resumo: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras were recently introduced as a trigonometric analogue of shifted twisted Yangians, whose truncations are expected to quantize fixed point loci in generalized affine Grassmannian slices. They are defined via a loop presentation with infinitely many generators and relations. candidatos.titulo: Classification of twisted Yangians as coideal subalgebras of Yangians
candidatos.autores: Kang Lu
candidatos.resumo: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a complex simple Lie algebra with an involution $ω$. We classify the homogeneous right coideal subalgebras of the Yangian of $\mathfrak g$ whose classical limit is the enveloping algebra of the twisted current algebra, embedded in the standard way, without assuming any formula for the coaction. For nontrivial $ω$, they form a family parametrized by a spectral parameter and an element of the center of the fixed-point subalgebra; for $ω=\mathrm{id}$, only a spectral parameter occurs. All members of the family are isomorphic as graded algebras, through explicit isomorphisms.

candidatos.titulo: Noise-shaped Sampling and Annealing for Scalable On-the-edge Training of Binary and Ternary AI Models
candidatos.autores: Zihao Chen, Zhili Xiao, Rui-Jie Zhu, Yipeng Wang, Jason Eshraghian, Shantanu Chakrabartty

candidatos.titulo: Unfragmenting Nawatl NMT: Single-Variant Specialization for Masewalkopa
candidatos.autores: Luis A. Mercado-Campos, Alexis Palmer
candidatos.resumo: In minoritized (low-resource) language technologies, a common response to data sparsity is to aggregate text across multiple varieties and treat the combined data as a single corpus. However, mixed corpora of closely related indigenous variants can produce an artificial register that is accountable to no single speaker community, a structural failure we call variant fragmentation. This issue is acute for minoritized languages native to Mexico, such as Nawatl. candidatos.titulo: HyCo: Hybrid Drafting for Cost-Efficient Mobile-Cloud Speculative Decoding
candidatos.autores: Hanbin Bae, Heejin Choi, Joohyung Lee, Byoung Jin Choi, Sangjun Park, Hoon-Young Cho
candidatos.resumo: Device-cloud speculative decoding reduces server computation, but growing a deep draft tree with a small language model (SLM) requires repeated passes on a mobile neural processing unit (NPU). We present HyCo, which runs the server model's native multi-token prediction (MTP) head on the device to build a deep chain and uses one SLM pass to add alternative branches. The server returns the hidden state, input embedding, and key-value entries needed by the head instead of executing its sequential steps. candidatos.titulo: CertEx: Exact Visual Retrieval at Scale by Certified Exclusion
candidatos.autores: Dongfang Zhao
candidatos.resumo: Exact $k$-nearest-neighbor (kNN) search over image descriptors and embeddings underlies visual retrieval, near-duplicate detection, the evaluation of learned representations, and increasingly the memory of LLM agents. However, exhaustive search computes every distance at full precision, whereas approximate indexes return recall below one. candidatos.titulo: What You Sign Is Not What You Run: The Verifiability Gap in Quantized LLM Supply Chains
candidatos.autores: Wei-Liang Liu, Cheng-Yen Tsai
candidatos.resumo: Model signing authenticates the full-precision weights W an LLM is released with, yet users run a quantized artifact Q whose producing transformation is not uniquely determined under current disclosure. candidatos.titulo: MemCode: Discrete Semantic Representations for Long-Term Agent Memory
candidatos.autores: Xin Li, Liang Hu, Duoqian Miao, Ming Peng, Qi Zhang
candidatos.resumo: Long-term memory remains a fundamental bottleneck for large language model (LLM) agents across sessions. Existing systems typically adopt a write-then-retrieve paradigm, storing context-dependent dialogue fragments and retrieving them via nearest-neighbor search in a continuous embedding space. This design yields unstable access units and systematically misses logically related but lexically distant evidence. candidatos.titulo: Attention via Black-Box Vector Search
candidatos.autores: Stepan Zharkov, Krish Singal, Ashwin Padaki, Alexandr Andoni
candidatos.resumo: Sparse attention mechanisms estimate attention over $n$ tokens using a small subset of keys. Many existing approaches use maximum inner product search (MIPS) to retrieve the heaviest keys, which motivates the following question: given black-box access to a MIPS oracle, how many keys must be retrieved to output an $\varepsilon$-accurate attention estimate? candidatos.titulo: Index-Free Dynamic Edge Retrieval with Energy-Tail-Aware Partial Scans
candidatos.autores: Mohammad Arif Rasyidi, Omar Alhussein
candidatos.resumo: Dynamic maximum inner-product search (MIPS) returns the $K$ stored vectors with the largest dot products with a query while allowing the dataset to change through insertions, replacements, and deletions. For edge retrieval, the challenge is to achieve high recall and fast queries without making updates expensive. candidatos.titulo: Time-Decayed Vector Search in the Rhythm of TANGO: Jointly Modeling Semantic Similarity and Temporal Freshness
candidatos.autores: Jiuqi Wei, Qiyao Luo, Quanqing Xu, Chuanhui Yang, Themis Palpanas

However, in a growing range of applications, relevance may evolve over time, making temporal freshness an additional signal beyond semantic similarity. In this paper, we formalize time-decayed vector search (TDVS), which incorporates continuous temporal decay into the search objective so that relevance is jointly determined by semantic similarity and temporal freshness. candidatos.titulo: RSLM: Training-Free Vector Quantization for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
candidatos.autores: Rastislav Lenhardt, Teodora Dobos, Thomas Vecchiato, Jiri Isa, Igor Ginzburg

candidatos.titulo: Fast and Efficient Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search for High-Dimensional LLM Embeddings
candidatos.autores: Nico Hezel, Kai Uwe Barthel, Bruno Schilling, Konstantin Schall, Andre Moelle, Klaus Jung

candidatos.titulo: Accelerating LLM Inference via Vector Index Based Output Embeddings
candidatos.autores: Martin Loretz, Sepp Hochreiter
candidatos.resumo: Large output embedding matrices create a significant memory bandwidth bottleneck during autoregressive decoding, especially for compact LLMs with large multilingual vocabularies. We reformulate the output projection followed by top-k token selection as a maximum inner product search over token embeddings and replace the dense vocabulary projection with an HNSW-based vector index. candidatos.titulo: Amortized Maximum Inner Product Search with Learned Support Functions
candidatos.autores: Theo X. Olausson, João Monteiro, Michal Klein, Marco Cuturi
candidatos.resumo: Maximum inner product search (MIPS) is a crucial subroutine in machine learning, requiring the identification of a vector taken within a database (the keys) that best aligns with a given query. We propose amortized MIPS: a regression-based approach that trains neural networks to directly predict MIPS solutions, amortizing the cost of repeatedly solving MIPS for queries drawn from a known distribution over a fixed key database. Our key insight is that the MIPS value function is the \emph{support} function of the set of keys, a well-studied convex function whose gradient yields the optimal key.

candidatos.autores: Han Chen, Steven Zhu, Yingrui Li

We introduce STARS, a transformer-based sequential recommendation framework built for large-scale, low-latency ecommerce settings. candidatos.titulo: Large Language Models Meet Extreme Multi-label Classification: Scaling and Multi-modal Framework
candidatos.autores: Diego Ortego, Marlon Rodríguez, Mario Almagro, Kunal Dahiya, David Jiménez, Juan C. SanMiguel

Queries in XMC are associated with relevant labels from extremely large label spaces, where it is critical to strike a balance between efficiency and performance. candidatos.titulo: SINDI: An Efficient Index for Sparse Vector Approximate Maximum Inner Product Search
candidatos.autores: Ruoxuan Li, Xiaoyao Zhong, Jiabao Jin, Peng Cheng, Wangze Ni, Zhitao Shen
candidatos.resumo: Sparse vector Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS) is crucial in multi-path retrieval for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Recent inverted index-based and graph-based algorithms have achieved high search accuracy with practical efficiency. However, their performance in production environments is often limited by redundant distance computations and frequent random memory accesses. candidatos.titulo: VIBE: Vector Index Benchmark for Embeddings
candidatos.autores: Elias Jääsaari, Ville Hyvönen, Matteo Ceccarello, Teemu Roos, Martin Aumüller
candidatos.resumo: Approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search is a performance-critical component of many machine learning pipelines, and rigorous benchmarking is essential for assessing the performance of vector indexes for ANN search. However, the datasets of existing benchmarks no longer represent modern ANN applications, creating a need for an up-to-date benchmark. candidatos.titulo: Stitching Inner Product and Euclidean Metrics for Topology-aware Maximum Inner Product Search
candidatos.autores: Tingyang Chen, Cong Fu, Xiangyu Ke, Yunjun Gao, Yabo Ni, Anxiang Zeng
candidatos.resumo: Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS) is a fundamental challenge in machine learning and information retrieval, particularly in high-dimensional data applications. Existing approaches to MIPS either rely solely on Inner Product (IP) similarity, which faces issues with local optima and redundant computations, or reduce the MIPS problem to the Nearest Neighbor Search under the Euclidean metric via space projection, leading to topology destruction and information loss. Despite the divergence of the two paradigms, we argue that there is no inherent binary opposition between IP and Euclidean metrics.

candidatos.autores: Daichi Amagata, Kazuyoshi Aoayama, Keito Kido, Sumio Fujita

Given an item vector (i.e., query), it retrieves all user vectors such that their $k$-MIPS results contain the item vector. Consider the cardinality of a reverse $k$-MIPS result. candidatos.titulo: Maximum Inner Product is Query-Scaled Nearest Neighbor
candidatos.autores: Tingyang Chen, Cong Fu, Kun Wang, Xiangyu Ke, Yunjun Gao, Wenchao Zhou
candidatos.resumo: Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS) for high-dimensional vectors is pivotal across databases, information retrieval, and artificial intelligence. candidatos.autores: Zhutao Zhuang, Nong Xiao, Zhiguang Chen, Yue Yu
candidatos.resumo: Disk-based approximate nearest-neighbor search (ANNS) supports retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), search, recommendation, and advertising over corpora that exceed memory capacity. Existing ANNS research often focuses on vector search at small top-K, whereas industrial-scale applications require larger retrieval sets. candidatos.titulo: The Geometry of Hierarchical Navigation: Accuracy and Query Cost for Point Process Input
candidatos.autores: Shankar Bhamidi, Souvik Dhara, Lars Schroeder, Clara Stegehuis
candidatos.resumo: Large-scale information retrieval systems, including retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and recommendation engines, widely use multi-layered hierarchical data structures for ultra-fast approximate nearest-neighbor search in high-dimensional vector spaces. However, the geometric conditions that ensure accurate and efficient greedy navigation remain poorly understood. candidatos.titulo: RiftANN: Efficient Graph Traversal for Vector Search with RDMA-Based Memory Disaggregation
candidatos.autores: Qi Lin, Zhenyu Zhang, Jun Kong, Zhichao Cao

Passive RDMA-based disaggregated memory provides scalable capacity without memory-node computation, but conventional best-first search performs poorly in this setting. Fine-grained and unnecessary remote reads increase communication cost, while dependencies between candidate evaluation and subsequent expansion serialize traversal and leave CPUs idle. candidatos.titulo: RaBitQ-SSD: Split Codes and Pipelined I/O for SSD-Resident Vector Search
candidatos.autores: Yuexuan Xu, Jianyang Gao, Michael Norris, Alibek Zhakubayev, Pankaj Singh, Junjie Qi

The challenge is to reduce SSD reads and hide I/O latency through concurrent reads and overlap with computation. candidatos.titulo: Aker: Density-Aware Approximate Caching for Vector Search (Extended Version)
candidatos.autores: Sukjoon Oh, Minki Kang, Dohyun Kim, Baotong Lu, Jing Liu, Qianxi Zhang

candidatos.autores: Robert Krauthgamer, Asaf Petruschka, Nir Petruschka

candidatos.autores: Yuemeng Xu, Zongxi Liu, Junyu Long, Yiming Huang, Jiarui Guo, Yangyujia Wang

candidatos.autores: Kwun Hang Lau, Ruiyuan Zhang, Elton Chun-Chai Li, Wun Yu Chan, Xiaojun Cheng, Xiaofang Zhou

Entropy coding supports finer rates, yet the achieved size depends on the quantized weight distribution and coding overhead. candidatos.autores: Yhonatan Kvich, Yonina C. Eldar
